headline: Every ready meal checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: With soups, curries and plated meals going into similar trays, the label is what tells one meal from the next. Here's what a camera check could look like on your tray line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every tray has its film on, sealed all the way round, with no food caught in the seal. A leaking meal tray is the kind of fault that comes back as a customer complaint.
labelLede: A beef casserole and a chicken curry look much the same through the film, and the wrong label can mean a missed allergen. The camera checks every tray carries the right label for the recipe, straight and intact.
codeLede: Fresh ready meals have a short use-by window, so the date has to be right on every tray. The system reads the printed date and batch code and compares them with the meal and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Glove pieces, film offcuts and loose parts can end up close to the line. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a case.

vocab.c1h: Film on and sealed all round
vocab.wrongCode: Wrong month: OCT printed, NOV expected
vocab.alert: Four creased seals in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the tray sealer.
